claims.statement: For a finite integer-complex endotactic network with rational positive rate bounds and a rational positive stoichiometric-class representative, the internally reconstructed N33 finite-affine-minimum proof yields a compact positive relative polytope with a strict inward margin on every relative facet; a sufficiently narrow collar preserves a positive margin, and the polytope can be rationally perturbed while preserving strictness.
assumptions: N33 affine-minimum and weighted essential-source drift reconstruction is correct
All reaction complexes are integer and nonnegative
Rates range pointwise in a supplied rational box [kappa,K] with kappa>0
The affine class has an exact rational description
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a bridge from the supplied N33 proof artifact to an N35-shaped certificate; it is not external validation, priority, or a useful-size construction bound.
claims.costs: Direct N33 coefficient acquisition has no usable bounds on scale, slopes, offsets, collar widths, or bit heights. Rational enumeration plus exact polynomial verification terminates under strict existence and rational input, but no general verifier was implemented here and no runtime or certificate-size bound is known.
claims.falsifier: A finite endotactic integer network and rational class/rate box for which the N33 active-slope proof holds but no strict relative facet collar exists, or a rational perturbation obstruction despite positive strict margins.
claims.next_gate: Implement and independently audit an exact rational verifier/acquirer for facet-collar inequalities, then submit the domain-erosion bridge and N33 base proof for external mathematical review.

claims.statement: Given an acquired strict rational inward-polytope certificate with margins gamma_i and collar widths ell_i, integer-volume factorial mass-action jumps with predictable bounded controls satisfy Pr(tau_Q<=T) <= sum_i exp(-theta_i V d_i) + 2 m V Lambda T exp(-c_* V), with V>=max(1,max_i ceil(2D_i/gamma_i)), theta_i=min(1/J_i,(gamma_i/2)/(3B_i)), c_*=min_i theta_i ell_i, and the constants defined in FINAL_REPORT.md.
assumptions: Integer nonnegative source complexes and integer stoichiometric jumps
Exact buffered lattice-compatible initial counts inside Q
Predictable rate control remains in the certified admissible set
The strict deterministic collar inequality holds for every allowed instantaneous rate vector
claims.novelty_boundary: Uses an elementary exponential-martingale certificate route consistent with established chemical jump large-deviation and exponential-Lyapunov methods; no optimal large-deviation exponent or all-time safety follows.
claims.costs: Factorial correction D_i/V, overshoot J_i/V, quadratic term B_i, activity Lambda, initial concentration gaps d_i, and horizon work O(V Lambda T) are charged explicitly.
claims.falsifier: An admissible lattice state/control within the stated bounds that violates the generator or stopped-Dynkin inequality, or a missing count-feasibility/factorial correction under the declared propensity convention.
claims.next_gate: External proof review and application-level acquisition of the lattice coset, rate envelope, and buffered start.

claims.statement: The common deterministic absorber and even a strict inward collar do not imply infinite-time molecular-jump safety: for A<->B with total count V and unit constant rates the finite irreducible chain exits [1/10,9/10] almost surely.
assumptions: Initial count is an interior state such as N_A=V/2 for even V
Both unimolecular reactions have rate one
claims.novelty_boundary: Refutes only the infinite-time safety implication, not the finite-exponential-horizon N35 bound.
claims.costs: No acquisition cost beyond the finite two-state reaction description and the finite irreducible birth-death chain.
claims.falsifier: Show that a finite irreducible continuous-time Markov chain on {0,...,V} can avoid its endpoint forever with positive probability; this contradicts recurrence of finite irreducible chains.
claims.next_gate: Retain finite-horizon confinement as the claim boundary.
